question: Will Olivia Chow win the 2026 Toronto mayoral election?
rules:
The 2026 Toronto mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 26, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Toronto as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Toronto.

evidence.excerpt: October 13, 2026 (Toronto, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Toronto survey finds Mayor Olivia Chow leading Brad Bradford 51% to 46% among decided and leaning voters, with 3% choosing someone else. Renters favour Chow 57% to 40%, while homeowners favour Bradford 50% to 45%. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Toronto residents from October 8 to October 9, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. For the total sample, the margin of error is +/- 3.1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

Chow still leads, but Bradford has cut her cushion to 3.5 points among decided voters. With 17 per cent undecided, Toronto’s race remains an open contest. CP24/CTV News Toronto/Nanos conducted a RDD dual frame (cell- and land-lines) hybrid random telephone and online survey of 757 residents of Toronto aged 18 years and over, from October 8th to October 10th, 2026. A random survey of 757 residents of Toronto is accurate ±3.6 percentage points, plus or minus, 19 times out of 20.

Advance voting in Toronto’s 2026 municipal election ended on Sunday, October 11 at 7 p.m. 222,550 eligible voters voted during six days of advance voting. Advance voting turnout in recent elections: 2023 Mayoral by-election – 129,745 votes; 2022 Toronto municipal election – 115,911 votes. Election day is Monday, October 26 from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

According to polling released by Forum Research Inc. after Tuesday night’s debate, Chow leads the mayoral race among decided and leaning voters with 46 per cent of support compared to Bradford, who follows with 42 per cent of support. The remaining results suggest that 12 per cent of respondents would vote for someone else. The poll was conducted on Oct. 6 through telephone surveys with 1,604 randomly selected Toronto residents over the age of 18. It carries a margin of error of 2.45 per cent, 19 times out of 20.

Toronto mayoral candidate Chris Alexander has pulled out of the race just weeks before election day. He made the announcement just a half hour before advance voting was set to begin in the city. Alexander has been polling a distant third in recent surveys behind incumbent Olivia Chow and Councillor Brad Bradford. In his announcement, he said he would not be endorsing any of the candidates and encouraged voters to read all the platforms and find the candidate that most aligns with you.

Half (47%) of Torontonians believe Mayor Olivia Chow deserves re-election, increasing 5 points since last year, and her approval rating is holding steady at six in ten (59%). Mayor Chow currently holds a 15-point lead over chief rival Brad Bradford in the horserace, but one quarter of likely voters remain undecided. These are the findings of an Ipsos survey conducted on behalf of the Toronto Star that was fielded between September 4 - 8, 2026. A total of n=1006 residents of Toronto aged 18+ participated in the survey which was fielded via the Ipsos’ panel.

The Toronto City Clerk has certified 361 candidates for the 2026 municipal election. The official list of certified candidates is available on the Toronto Elections List of Candidates & Third Party Advertisers webpage. Election day is Monday, October 26 from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Advance voting will be available from Tuesday, October 6 to Sunday, October 11 from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
